### Kalyan-Lankireddy__buildathon-sessions 2aa5f3d 11-20 21:50
v2.5 (experiment C): pread input into huge-page buffers, huge-page allocator with a reuse pool
Hypothesis: the scorer's extra time is page-fault cost on x86 (4 KB pages, many faults).
- Input is read with pread() in ~64 MB pieces, each into its own 2 MB-aligned buffer, and parsed
  right away while hot. No mmap of the input.
- A global allocator gives every allocation of 2 MB or more a 2 MB-aligned block with
  madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE). Allocations under 2 MB are untouched (the 256 per-chunk shard buffers
  are about 220 KB each, so they still use 4 KB pages).
- Freed big blocks are kept in a pool (cap 3 GB, fixed arrays, no allocation inside the allocator)
  and reused by later big allocations of similar size, so later stages skip page faults and zeroing.
- Dockerfile: back to -C target-cpu=x86-64-v3 (cascadelake build B is a separate commit, 83f1afd);
  explicit --target kept.

Gates passed (this exact code): 36/36 fixtures and make check-dev MATCH through the amd64 image;
20M seed 7 exact vs the DuckDB reference both native and through the image; stage-by-stage exact
on seeds 2, 3, 4 (1M) and 5 (5M); timestamp cross-check vs reference ts_ms; unit tests for
read_map (7 chunk sizes, empty/header-only/no-trailing-newline files) and the allocator.

Not benchmarked locally (the Mac cannot show THP effects); the scorer is the judge.
Memory: 20M peak 5.1 GB anon (v2.2: 4.46 GB incl. 1.8 GB mapped input). Expect about 15 GB at 60M.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

### bzells11__Mech-Bot-Repo- b1b77da 11-20 23:13

Run or stay now comes from the awareness picture instead of an HP line:

enemies that know where we are and are close enough to join, killed

### niranjankumarnk__mech-royale d308a0c 11-20 21:45
Experiment F: free-for-all package and sturdier navigation on top of E
Practice fighting, looting and upgrade order are experiment E's. Roof
play (experiment R, 2.40) is switched off.

Free-for-all side:
- recognise a free-for-all within seconds: one death we did not cause in
  the first 30 s (two later), or two of three softer signs
- then stay out of sight of every known mech, run to the nearest cover
  by walking distance when seen, loot only where nobody is looking,
  fight only with a clear advantage or a pursuer that will not let go
- behave that careful way for the first 20 s of every match

Navigation:
- walkability checked metre by metre on the terrain grid
- jump and jet over what holds the mech up (pressed against something,
  or 3 s without progress): gets it out of the stadium bowl

Behaviour switches are now a runtime Policy; the simulator can run
policies against each other and replay recorded matches as ghosts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
